page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.2-32 is a flexible virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at 2.7 GHz. It is provisioned with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, yielding 4 dedicated virtual CPUs alongside 32.0 GB of system RAM. This configuration provides a generous 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU, placing the resource profile into a memory-optimized tier.

Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent from this configuration, and the instance includes no local NVMe or SSD storage volumes. Persistent storage must be supplied via network-attached volumes. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the 4 vCPUs utilize dedicated CPU allocation, execution avoids performance degradation associated with shared or burstable CPU environments.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, provisioning 32 GB of RAM across only 2 physical cores allows workloads with high memory footprints to run without paying for surplus compute capacity. The qualitative balance favors applications that require large in-memory caches or buffering without demanding extensive core parallelization.

VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.2-32 is suitable for memory-intensive operational workloads, including in-memory caching systems, intermediate relational database servers, extract-transform-load data preprocessing jobs, and web applications with substantial working sets.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.2-32 is an x86_64 compute instance utilizing AMD EPYC 9J45 processors clocked at 2.7 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, delivering 4 dedicated virtual CPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio providing 8.0 GB of memory per virtual thread, this configuration emphasizes memory capacity relative to compute density. The server contains no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on network storage solutions for persistent data needs. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated vCPU provisioning ensures predictable execution without hypervisor-level core sharing. Due to its elevated memory-to-core balance, the VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.2-32 instance is aligned with memory-constrained workloads such as in-memory caching layers, transactional database management systems, search index nodes, and backend application services requiring moderate processing capacity alongside extensive RAM buffers.
